editorial: Young detective Enola Holmes is back, and this time she is running her own agency in Victorian London. Business is slow until a poor matchstick factory girl goes missing, pulling Enola into a dangerous case full of secrets, corrupt bosses, and hidden clues. Along the way she reunites with her famous brother Sherlock, her friend Tewkesbury, and a few new allies. The movie keeps the same playful energy as the first film, mixing quick humor with real danger and a warm family heart. Millie Bobby Brown carries the story with charm and confidence, and Henry Cavill gets more to do as Sherlock. The action scenes are fun, the mystery keeps you guessing, and the period setting looks great. Some jokes land better than others, and a few plot twists feel a bit rushed near the end. Still, it is a lively, feel-good adventure that works for teens and adults alike.
endingExplained: In the final act, Enola discovers the missing girl Sarah is alive and that the matchstick factory bosses were poisoning workers with phosphorus. The true villain is Mira Troy, who reveals herself as Moriarty and escapes after a rooftop chase. Sherlock and Enola team up to stop her, but she gets away. Enola solves the case, clears Sarah's name, and decides to keep working as a detective. The movie ends with Sherlock and Enola hinting at future cases together, setting up more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mystery adventures with a strong female lead
